# Changes from upstream draw.io

Diagrams is a fork of [draw.io](https://github.com/jgraph/drawio), licensed
under the Apache License 2.0. This file records modifications made to the
original work, as required by Section 4(b) of that License.

**Fork point:** upstream commit `074a2ea4`, draw.io version 31.4.2.

Individual modified files also carry a change notice in their header, in the
form:

    Modified <YYYY-MM-DD> by Hossein Oliabak as part of Diagrams.
    Changes from the original are licensed under the Apache License 2.0.

## Modifications

| Date | Area | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-03 | Build | Upgraded the bundled Closure Compiler in `etc/build/compiler.jar` from v20220502 to v20260831. Verified: `ant app` builds with 0 errors and 0 warnings, and the resulting bundle boots with 0 console errors and 0 failed requests. Output grew 3,820 bytes (+0.04%). |
| 2026-09-03 | Branding | Rebranded to Diagrams: `index.html` (title, meta, canonical, splash), `images/manifest.json`, `images/browserconfig.xml`, `clear.html`, and a new icon set generated from `etc/branding/`. Theme colour #d89000 -> #22176F. |
| 2026-09-03 | Branding | Replaced 5,083 value-side occurrences of "draw.io" with "Diagrams" across all 59 `resources/dia*.txt` locale files, and 58 `app.diagrams.net` URLs with `diagrams.oliabak.com`. Resource *keys* (including the key literally named `draw.io`) are unchanged. |
| 2026-09-03 | Branding | `Editor.prototype.appName` -> `Diagrams` (this drives `document.title`). Template-picker category label -> `Diagrams`. The 18 internal `getServiceName() == 'draw.io'` deployment checks are deliberately left alone: they are an internal discriminator, never user-visible. |
| 2026-09-03 | Privacy | Removed upstream's hard-coded telemetry hosts in `js/diagramly/Init.js`, which set `window.DRAWIO_LOG_URL` to `log.diagrams.net` / `log.draw.io` via a hostname *suffix* match. This fork sends no telemetry. |
| 2026-09-03 | Links | Repointed Help menu targets that implied an upstream service relationship: `support` (was `github.com/jgraph/drawio/wiki/Getting-Support`), `downloadDesktop` (was `get.diagrams.net`), Electron `website` (was `drawio.com`), and the remote `shortcuts.svg` fallback. Removed upstream's YouTube walkthrough from both Help menus. |
| 2026-09-03 | Attribution | Added an About dialog. Upstream renders only a version label; this fork opens a dialog carrying the Apache 2.0 attribution, links to the upstream project and licence, and the trademark disclaimer. Built with `textContent`, links carry `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. |
| 2026-09-03 | Fix | Added the missing `images/mstile-150x150.png`, referenced by `browserconfig.xml` but never shipped upstream (a 404 on every load). |
| 2026-09-03 | Backends | Disabled Dropbox, OneDrive/SharePoint and GitLab via `urlParams` in `js/PreConfig.js` rather than by deleting files, keeping the fork cheap to rebase. Trello was already off by default. Verified: File > Open from / Import from now offer only Browser, Device and URL. |
| 2026-09-03 | Security | Removed five hard-coded upstream OAuth identities that this fork would otherwise have authenticated with: draw.io's Google client ID and app ID (`js/diagramly/DriveClient.js`), and its GitHub App, Dropbox and GitLab IDs plus a second Google client (`js/diagramly/Init.js`). All now default to null. |
| 2026-09-03 | Privacy | Repointed two endpoints that silently sent user content to third parties. `EXPORT_URL` defaulted to `convert.diagrams.net/node/export` and `VSS_CONVERT_URL` to `convert.diagrams.net/VsdConverter/api/converter`; both now target same-origin paths that are not served, so the features fail closed instead of uploading. `DRAWIO_LIGHTBOX_URL` moved off `viewer.diagrams.net`. |
| 2026-09-03 | Verified | Network egress test: loaded the app, drew on the canvas and opened the storage menus. Only origin contacted was the local server; zero external requests, zero page errors. |
| 2026-09-03 | Deploy | Added `build-dist.sh`, which copies only what production serves into `dist/`: 133 MB and 3,083 files, down from 155 MB and 3,411. Excludes `WEB-INF/` (whose placeholder `*_client_secret` files must never be published), the unminified dev sources, and the disabled backends' pages. The fork keeps upstream's full tree so rebases stay clean. Verified: the trimmed tree boots with zero external requests, zero failed requests and zero errors. |
| 2026-09-03 | Desktop | Built a macOS application from this fork via drawio-desktop, whose submodule pins the same upstream commit. Bundle id `com.oliabak.diagrams`, own icon, copyright carrying the draw.io attribution. Registered as an Alternate handler for .drawio so an existing draw.io install keeps the default association. |
| 2026-09-03 | Desktop fix | The desktop app quit instantly on launch. Upstream's `package.json` has `name: \"draw.io\"`, so Electron used `~/Library/Application Support/draw.io`, the same profile as an installed draw.io, and `requestSingleInstanceLock()` failed whenever the real app was running. Added `productName: \"Diagrams\"` so it gets its own profile and the two coexist. |
| 2026-09-03 | Desktop fix | electron-builder with `identity: null` leaves the bundle carrying Electron's linker signature while rewriting Info.plist, which Apple Silicon refuses to launch. `build-mac.sh` ad-hoc re-signs after packaging; the bundle then validates and satisfies its Designated Requirement. |
| 2026-09-03 | Scope | Dropped the hosted deployment. There is no `diagrams.oliabak.com`: `DRAWIO_LIGHTBOX_URL` now points at an unserved same-origin path so the lightbox fails closed, keyboard shortcuts always load locally, the canonical link points at the tool page, and 58 locale references to the dead subdomain were repointed. |
| 2026-09-03 | Install | Installed to `/Applications/Diagrams.app`, verified launching with its own renderer alongside an existing `/Applications/draw.io.app`. |
| 2026-09-03 | Legal | Added `NOTICE` and this `CHANGES.md` to satisfy Apache License 2.0 Section 4. |
| 2026-09-04 | Shapes | Added the Oliabak shape library, this fork's own palette. `shapes/mxOliabak.js` defines three new shapes under the `mxgraph.oliabak.*` namespace, which upstream does not use: `arc` (a connector drawn as one cubic Bezier with a single draggable bow handle), `scurve` (the same curve with two independent handles) and `tunnel` (a see-through tube swept along a bowed centre line, for drawing a VPN tunnel over a topology). Upstream has no adjustable curved connector at all: `curved=1` only smooths a route that already has waypoints, so a two-point edge stays straight. |
| 2026-09-04 | Shapes | `js/diagramly/sidebar/Sidebar-Oliabak.js` adds seven palettes: `Oliabak` (expanded, the three curve and pipe presets plus 20 core devices) and six collapsed catalogue sections covering 117 classic network devices. The devices are drawn by the stencils already in the fork (`stencils/cisco/*.xml`); only the preset style is new, a grey body with red markings rather than upstream's blue. Nothing is redrawn or copied, so the diagrams still open in stock draw.io and a rebase cannot conflict with the palette. |
| 2026-09-04 | Shapes | Every colour in the device preset stays editable per shape. `fillColor` and `strokeColor` are the body and outline; `strokeColor2` (inner markings) and `fillColor2` (antennas) are style keys the stencils themselves read, so draw.io surfaces them in Format > Style without any extra code, the marking colour as a `Stroke (2)` picker. The three new shapes declare `customProperties`, listing Bend Angle, Pipe Width, Start Angle, Shading, Open End and Curvature in Format > Property. |
| 2026-09-04 | Shapes | Reworked `curvedPipe` into `tunnel` for illustrating a VPN tunnel over a topology. The tube is now swept along a cubic centre line bowed by `tunnelBow`, where zero is a straight run, so one handle covers straight and curved instead of a bend angle that could never reach zero. Both ends are stroked ellipses with no fill, so the tunnel reads as see-through and the whole shape stays a single filled layer, which the half-transparent default (`fillOpacity=50`) needs: stacked translucent fills would show as darker patches. Round-tube shading is one gradient for the same reason. The outline traces the outer half of each opening rather than a flat chord, without which the ellipse enclosed a sliver of bare background. `curvedPipe` stays registered as an alias so anything drawn under the old name still opens. |
| 2026-09-04 | SmartArt | Added `mxgraph.oliabak.arcChevron`, one slice of a ring with a chevron head and a matching notch in the tail so slices interlock. The circle comes from the cell bounds, not the slice, so every stage of a ring is identical geometry differing only in `startAngle`. The label runs along the slice's own arc through an SVG `textPath`, the technique the fork already uses for `curvedText`, and flips in the lower half so it stays upright. Three handles: sweep, ring width, chevron depth. |
| 2026-09-04 | SmartArt | Added `mxgraph.oliabak.infinity`, the DevOps figure eight. Built from two circles joined by their two internal tangents, which cross at the midpoint between the centres. Each tangent is given a whole stage, so the crossing lands in the middle of a stage rather than on a joint, the way the mark is drawn: release passes over plan at the centre of both bands. An earlier lemniscate version was dropped because its self-intersection is a single point on one curve, so the bands met there instead of crossing through one another. |
| 2026-09-04 | SmartArt | The loop and the ring are containers (`mxgraph.oliabak.infinity`, `mxgraph.oliabak.cycle`) whose stages are ordinary child cells, one per stage. Each stage is fully editable on its own: moved, resized, recoloured, relabelled (double-click) and deleted, and each carries its own three drag handles (band width or ring width, chevron depth, label position). The arrangement is the point, so the stages are deliberately not locked parts. The container's Format panel carries a **Stages** field, and a model listener, installed on first paint, reacts to just two things: the container's own style (a count change reflows the figure, any other parameter propagates to the children) and a stage added or removed by hand (the count is corrected and the figure reflowed). Moving or recolouring one stage never triggers it. reflow takes the target count explicitly so it is never tripped by a stale style cache mid-edit. |
| 2026-09-04 | SmartArt | `Oliabak / SmartArt` palette: cycles at 3/4/5/6/8 stages, DevOps loops at 8 and 6, chevron processes and step boxes at 3/4/5/6 steps (straight chevrons reuse draw.io's own `step` shape), and the bare arc chevron. |
| 2026-09-04 | SmartArt | Each stage now gets a cell box that hugs the stage instead of spanning the whole figure, so its selection outline and resize handles belong to it rather than wrapping the entire diagram. The stage records its fractional position within the figure as `segBox`, and rebuilds the figure's frame from its own bounds at paint time. Moving a stage moves its frame with it; resizing a stage scales its frame, which is what makes one chevron independently resizable, at the cost of it no longer matching its neighbours' curvature. A deferred normalise pass on first paint gives boxes to palette presets and to diagrams saved before this, since a preset builds its stages before the group enters the model and so reports no child change. |
| 2026-09-04 | SmartArt | Dropped `container=1` from the loop and ring presets. It made the child stages directly clickable, which left the group itself unselectable, so the whole figure could not be picked up or resized again after the drop. As a plain group draw.io's drill-down applies: the first click selects the figure (resizable, and `recursiveResize=1` scales the stages with it), the second selects one stage. |
| 2026-09-04 | Desktop fix | The app could not be quit and needed a Force Quit. `drawio-desktop`'s window `close` handler unconditionally calls `event.preventDefault()` and completes the close only when the renderer answers an `isModified` message. A renderer that is gone, has crashed, or whose reply is dropped by the guards on `isModified-result` can never answer, leaving a window that cannot be closed and an app that cannot be quit. Fixed in `src/main/electron.js`: a close is now let through untouched when the webContents is null, destroyed or crashed, and an otherwise-unanswered handshake is closed by a 3 second watchdog. The watchdog tracks the id of the last answered handshake (`lastIsModifiedReplyId`), so a save dialog the user cancelled is left alone and unsaved work is never discarded. Verified: quit with a window open, quit after closing the window (the case that used to wedge), and quit straight after launch all exit cleanly, leaving no singleton lock behind. |
| 2026-09-04 | Desktop fix | The desktop app was silently running as a browser build: File then Save as offered the browser's Download and Open in New Window instead of a native macOS save panel, and it never remembered the last save location. `js/bootstrap.js` sets `mxIsElectron` only when the user agent contains both `' electron/'` and `' draw.io/'`. The second token is Electron's `productName`, which the 2026-09-03 rebranding changed to `Diagrams`, so the test failed and `js/diagramly/DesktopLibrary.js` and `js/diagramly/ElectronApp.js` were never loaded. Fixed by accepting either product name, in `js/bootstrap.js`, `js/export.js` and `js/vsdxImporter.js`, which all carry the same check. Verified in the packaged app over the remote debugging port: `mxIsElectron` is now true, the user agent token is `Diagrams/31.4.2`, both desktop scripts load, and the app mode is `device` rather than `browser`. |
| 2026-09-04 | Shapes | Added `mxgraph.oliabak.router` and `mxgraph.oliabak.switch`, drawn from parameters rather than stencilled. The Cisco stencils bake their perspective into fixed paths, so resizing distorts them: a stretched router becomes a capsule and a stretched switch becomes a wedge. The router takes `size` as its lid depth, following draw.io's own cylinder convention exactly (pixels, clamped, handle on the left edge at `y + size`), so the gesture is the one people already know. The switch has two, because an isometric box has two independent offsets and collapsing them into one made the top face and the depth impossible to set separately: `size` is how tall the top face reads and rides the left edge, `depth` is how far back the box goes and rides the top edge, so the two gestures cannot be confused. The markings are the stencils' own arrow polygons, re-expressed in the face's own axes: the router's on the unit circle of the lid ellipse, the switch's along the top face's two edges. They therefore foreshorten and shear with the face instead of floating over it. Both fill their arrows without stroking, as the stencils do, because the arrows are only a few pixels thick once foreshortened and any visible outline swamps them. |
| 2026-09-09 | Shapes | Added `Oliabak / Annotations`, first in the sidebar: brackets, braces, dimension lines and the arrows used for labelling. Most entries are draw.io's own shapes gathered rather than rebuilt. `curlyBracket` existed but appeared in General as two vertical entries only, and `dimension` was buried in Floorplan; both already work in any direction, so what was missing was the orientations and one place to find them. Only the square span bracket is new, as `mxgraph.oliabak.bracket` and a stemmed variant `bracketStem`, because draw.io has no square bracket at all. Both are built on `mxActor` the way `CurlyBracketShape` is, so the stock `rounded` and `arcSize` styles round the corners and `direction` turns them to face any way without a second shape. Height is the depth of the returns, so resizing sets the tick length. |
| 2026-09-09 | Shapes | Added `textRotation`, an absolute label angle in degrees that is independent of the shape's own rotation, in `js/grapheditor/Graph.js` beside the existing `labelAutoRotate` override, and offered on every shape through `Editor.commonProperties`. A label otherwise inherits its shape's rotation with no way to opt out, which makes annotation awkward: a bracket turned on its side to mark a column still wants a level label, and that angle is unrelated to the bracket's. Absent means inherit, so nothing already drawn changes. Verified: with the key unset a 45 degree shape still labels at 45; set to 0 the same shape labels level; set to -30 on a 45 degree shape the label is at -30. |
| 2026-09-11 | Shapes | The tunnel's mouths are a layer of their own. A tunnel now has a locked companion cell, `mxgraph.oliabak.tunnelMouths`, that fills just the two openings, in a darker shade of the tunnel's fill by default (Format > Property > Interior; `none` restores the see-through holes). It follows the tunnel's bounds, style and parent, sits below it, and is never selectable, so it behaves as part of the tunnel. This is what gives a tunnel depth in the z-order: whatever is sent behind the mouths is hidden by them, whatever lies between the mouths and the tunnel shows in the openings and is hidden by the wall, whatever is above the tunnel is on top. Before this the openings were true holes and a router sent to the back still showed through them. A new companion goes to the bottom of its layer rather than just under the tunnel, so everything already drawn stays in front of it: a line already through the tube keeps showing in the mouths, and only what is sent to back from then on goes behind. The sync hooks `BEFORE_UNDO`, as upstream's own style sync does, so the companion's changes join the edit that caused them and one undo reverts both; a pasted group carrying a copied companion has it adopted by the copied tunnel. Verified: drop, move, undo and redo, curvature and fill changes, interior colour and `none`, delete and undo, clone, group clone, and a pixel check that a red block sent to back is hidden in the mouth while a line brought between shows there and is hidden under the wall. |
| 2026-09-11 | Shapes | Added `Oliabak / Connectivity`, the physical layer, in a second shape file `shapes/mxOliabakConnectivity.js` under `mxgraph.oliabak.conn.*`. draw.io ships nothing for it: no cable types, no connectors, no NICs, and only three port-row glyphs for pluggables at rack scale. Nine shapes, all drawn from parameters so a palette entry is only a starting value of a live property: `pluggable` (GBIC, SFP, SFP+, SFP28, QSFP+, QSFP28, QSFP-DD, OSFP; form factor picks the apertures, latch, heatsink ridges and face depth, each also settable on its own), `connector` (LC, SC, ST, MPO/MTP, RJ45, F-type, BNC, duplex where that exists, boot length on a handle), `patchCable` (an icon with a plug at each end, sagging or coiled between them, strands and both plugs chosen from the media), `cable` (an edge), `port` (a socket face on, or a row of them), `nic` (PCIe with the ports on the bracket, or OCP 3.0), `patchPanel` (ears, label strip, grouped port rows), `mediaConverter` and `coupler` (bulkhead adapters, keystones and barrels). Sixty palette entries. |
| 2026-09-11 | Shapes | Cables come twice over. As an edge (`mxgraph.oliabak.conn.cable`, built on `mxConnector` so routing, waypoints and arrowheads are stock) the jacket is `strokeColor` and its thickness `strokeWidth`, so the Line controls do what they say, and a darker outline is drawn under it so the jacket reads as a tube on any background. The presets carry the jacket colours the media actually come in: OS2 yellow, OM1/OM2 orange, OM3/OM4 aqua, OM5 lime, copper blue, coax black, DAC and AOC dark. A plug can be drawn at each end, turned to follow the last segment, its length on a handle that drags back along the cable. As an icon (`patchCable`) the cable follows the grey and red family, for a legend or a bill of materials, with the real colour one property away. |
| 2026-09-11 | Shapes | The classic device preset's body grey is lifted from `#B3B3B3` to `#C8C8C8`, across the stencilled devices, the parametric router and switch, and the new connectivity set, for more contrast under the red markings. |
| 2026-09-11 | Shapes | One plug painter serves the connector shape, both ends of the cable icon and both ends of the cable edge. It draws in a local frame whose x axis may run either way (a plug pointing left or right) and, for an edge, inside a rotation about the end point, so the plug has one definition and appears at any angle. Port faces are shared the same way between the port shape, the patch panel, the NIC bracket and the media converter, and keep their natural aspect ratio in a cell taller than they are rather than stretching to fill it. |
| 2026-09-11 | Shapes | Wiring: `Editor.js` registers `mxStencilRegistry.libraries['oliabak/conn']` for on-demand loading, `Sidebar-Oliabak.js` adds the palette after the everyday one, and `Sidebar.js` lists it in More Shapes. Verified on the compiled bundle: all sixty entries render, every shape lists its properties in Format > Property and offers its handles (two on the NIC and the cable icon, one elsewhere), zero console errors. |
| 2026-09-11 | Branding | Icon redrawn as three bands in the lion and sun colours, green over white over red, with a small gold network across the middle band: a hub and two leaves drawn as rings on links. The bands are clipped to the rounded tile so they meet its corners cleanly. The small mark for 16 and 32px keeps the bands and reduces the network to a single gold dot, which is all a tile that size can carry. Every raster size, the favicon, the maskable variants and the desktop iconset are regenerated from these two files. |
| 2026-09-10 | Shapes | Added `mxgraph.oliabak.cylinderLabel`: text wrapped onto a cylinder's surface, in `Oliabak / Annotations`. A cylinder of radius R seen from the side projects a surface point at angle t to `x = R sin t` and foreshortens it by `cos t`, so characters laid at even angles land at sine-spaced positions, bunching towards the rim on their own, and each is squashed by the cosine of where it sits. Angles are handed out in proportion to each character's measured width, through a cached canvas context, so an l takes less of the drum than a W; spreading them evenly is what gives most faked barrel text away. Wrap span and curve both have handles, on different edges so they cannot be confused. Unfilled and unstroked by default, to be laid over an existing cylinder or tunnel. |
| 2026-09-10 | Shapes | The tunnel is flat by default. The round-tube gradient read as decoration next to solid shapes and fought a fill chosen deliberately, so Shading now defaults to 0 and the fill is drawn solid. The property is still there to raise where the tube should look round. |
| 2026-09-10 | Fix | The tunnel's end-face handle sat outside the shape's left edge, at mid-height, under draw.io's own left connection arrow, so hovering it produced the arrow instead and the handle could not be grabbed. The unit tangent along the tube is (n.y, -n.x) and it was being negated, sending the handle out of the tube rather than into it. It is also held off the centre line now, since the west resize handle and that connection arrow both sit at mid-height and the shallowest depth brings it close to the edge. Measured: inside the shape at every depth, and 17px clear of the west resize handle at its closest. |
| 2026-09-10 | Fix | The tunnel's end openings were traced in the same winding as the outline, so the nonzero fill rule filled them instead of leaving them empty and they rendered as solid faces. Reversed. Verified against a block of colour placed behind the shape, which now shows through both openings; a connector run through the tube is visible in each mouth and hidden along the wall between them. |
| 2026-09-10 | Shapes | The tunnel is opaque by default. The openings only mean anything if the wall hides what runs inside the tube, and the previous half transparency showed a connector the whole way through, which defeated them. Set Fill Opacity by hand where the topology underneath matters more. |
| 2026-09-10 | Shapes | The end-face handle covered its whole range in about twenty pixels and was unusable. The mouth is inset by half the tube thickness times the depth, so it slid along with the handle and cancelled part of the travel; the track now adds that radius back, giving roughly eighty pixels of real movement whatever the tube's size. |
| 2026-09-10 | Shapes | The tunnel's two end faces are now adjustable and behave like openings. Their foreshortening was a constant in code; it is a style, `tunnelEndDepth`, with a handle on the left mouth that drags along the tube axis, joining the curvature and width handles which both act on the body. The centre line is inset by however far the openings bulge, so a deep end face lands on the cell edge instead of hanging outside its own selection box. |
| 2026-09-10 | Shapes | The two openings are now holes in the tunnel's fill rather than faces drawn over it, traced against the outline's winding so the nonzero fill rule leaves them empty. This is what lets a connector read as passing through the tube: with the tunnel in front of the line, the wall hides the line along its length while both openings let it show, so it enters one end, disappears inside and comes out the other. Filled faces covered the line at exactly the two places it needed to be visible. |
| 2026-09-04 | Branding | Redrew the icon in the lion and sun colours on a white ground: a router (green, #319B42) over a switch (gold, #FFB81C) over a computer (red, #DA291C), linked as a three-node topology. Three stacked devices turn to mush at 16px, so `etc/branding/diagrams-mark-small.svg` carries a reduced silhouette mark, circle over square over rectangle in the same colours, which `regenerate-icons.py` now uses for the 16, 32 and 48px favicon sizes; 64px and up take the full drawing. |
| 2026-09-04 | Shapes | Wiring: `Sidebar.js` (`defaultEntries` now leads with `oliabak`, `initPalettes` builds it, `updateEntries` lists it first under Standard), `Devel.js` (`?dev=1` loading), `Editor.js` (`mxStencilRegistry.libraries['oliabak']` for on-demand loading), `etc/build/build.xml` (compiled into `sidebar.min.js`), and a generated `images/sidebar-oliabak.png` for the More Shapes dialog. Verified: production build boots with 0 console errors, 0 failed requests and 0 external requests; all seven palettes present; all three shapes and their handles registered. |
